newlyAudited.subject: the adjacency matrices inside AdjacentComponentMatrixTests
newlyAudited.eachIsAsserted: Every one is pinned by a require on cases.size(), so the figures are the code's own claims rather than my reading of loops.
newlyAudited.whyItMattersForRuntime: These 9 matrices live inside 8 @GameTest methods, which is why those methods carry timeoutTicks of 1000000 and dominate the suite's wall-clock time. The combination counts are the reason the full run takes hours.

aCoincidenceWorthFlagging.observation: The nine matrix combinations total 611, and the JUnit @Test declarations also number 611.
aCoincidenceWorthFlagging.theyAreUnrelated: One is a count of combinations inside the gametest source set; the other is a count of annotations in the test source set. Different sets, different meanings, no shared derivation.
aCoincidenceWorthFlagging.whyRecordIt: Two unrelated quantities landing on the same value in the same report invites a reader to assume one was computed from the other, or that one is a typo for the other. Naming the coincidence prevents that.

conclusion: Every numeric claim in the report now has a traced source. The one previously unexamined figure - the adjacency combinations - reconciles and turns out to explain the suite's runtime.
